product.description: Cel de-al Doilea Război Mondial a lăsat in urma lui o Europă in haos. Peisajele fuseseră distruse, oraşe intregi rase de pe faţa pămacirc;ntului şi mai mult de 35 de milioane de oameni ucişi. Pe cea mai mare parte din continent, instituţiile a căror existenţă o considerăm astăzi un lucru firesc ndash; cum ar fi poliţia, presa, transportul, administraţiile locale şi naţionale ndash; erau fie cu totul absente, fie compromise total. Rata criminalităţii ajunsese la niveluri extrem de ridicate, economia se prăbuşise, iar populaţia Europei se afla in pragul foametei. Icirc;n acest studiu inovator al anilor care au urmat conflagraţiei mondiale, Keith Lowe descrie un continent incă bacirc;ntuit de violenţă, unde mari părţi ale populaţiei trebuiau incă să accepte faptul că războiul se terminase. El scoate in evidenţă moralitatea deformată şi nevoia insaţiabilă de răzbunare care au reprezentat moştenirea acestui conflict. Descrie purificarea etnică şi războaiele civile care au distrus vieţile oamenilor obişnuiţi de la Marea Baltică la Mediterană şi intemeierea unei noi ordini mondiale care a adus, in cele din urmă, stabilitate, intr-un continent zguduit din temelii. Acestea au fost realităţi, ne spune autorul, care au existat pe tot continentul ndash; la Est şi la Vest. Bazacirc;ndu-se pe documente originale, pe interviuri şi literatură de specialitate in opt limbi diferite, Continentul barbar ne oferă o imagine a unei scurte perioade haotice dintre finalul celui de-al Doilea Război Mondial şi inceputul Războiului Rece. Cartea reprezintă o premieră, fiind prima lucrare importantă despre această perioadă. După ce a petrecut peste un deceniu lucracirc;nd ca editor, Keith Lowe este acum istoric şi autor de cărţi de istorie. Este recunoscut drept o autoritate in ceea ce priveşte cel de-al Doilea Război Mondial şi a fost invitat adesea la radio şi la TV, atacirc;t in Marea Britanie, cacirc;t şi in SUA. Este autorul apreciatei lucrări Inferno: The Devastation of Hamburg, 1943. Locuieşte in nordul Londrei, impreună cu soţia şi cei doi copii.

# Continentul Barbar (The Barbaric Continent) by Litera

## Unveiling the Chaos: A Study of Post-War Europe

Dive into **"Continentul barbar,"** an essential historical study from the renowned author Keith Lowe. This groundbreaking book offers a unique and necessary look at the period immediately following World War IIâa time when Europe was thrown into profound chaos.

The Second World War left a continent devastated: landscapes were destroyed, entire cities razed, and millions of lives were lost. But the devastation went deeper than buildings; it affected civilization itself. For vast areas of the continent, fundamental institutionsâsuch as police forces, reliable media, transportation networks, local and national administrationsâwere either entirely absent or severely compromised.

**"Continentul barbar"** provides an innovative examination of these years following the global conflict. Keith Lowe describes a Europe grappling with extreme violence, where much of the population was struggling to accept that the war had actually ended. The book powerfully highlights the distorted morality and the insatiable need for revenge that served as the lingering legacy of the conflict.

### What Does the Book Cover?

The narrative scope is immense, chronicling multiple devastating realties:

*   **Wartime Aftermath:** The breakdown of economies, soaring crime rates, and widespread hunger faced by European populations.
*   **Social Turmoil:** Detailed accounts of ethnic cleansing and civil wars that ravaged ordinary lives from the Baltic Sea to the Mediterranean.
*   **The Dawn of a New Order:** How stability eventually returned to the continent after this period of upheaval.

Drawing on original documents, interviews, and specialized literature in eight different languages, **"Continentul barbar"** offers an unparalleled image of this short, chaotic interregnumâthe time between the end of WWII and the beginning of the Cold War. It is noted as a premiere work, offering crucial insights into this pivotal period of history on both the East and West sides of the continent.

### About the Author: Keith Lowe

Keith Lowe brings immense authority to his subject matter. After spending over a decade working as an editor, he established himself as a highly regarded historian specializing in World War II. His expertise has earned him recognition across the UK, Canada, and the USA, where he has been invited to speak on radio and television multiple times. He is also the author of the acclaimed work, *Inferno: The Devastation of Hamburg, 1943*.

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Q: Is this book primarily about the fighting during WWII?**
A: No. While it covers the aftermath of World War II, its focus is specifically on the chaotic period *after* the warâthe years leading up to and encompassing the start of the Cold War.

**Q: Is "Continentul barbar" recommended for casual readers or experts?**
A: The book is comprehensive and deeply researched, drawing from multiple languages and sources. While its historical depth makes it suitable for serious students of history, its narrative structure aims to make these complex events accessible to a wider audience interested in 20th-century European history.
